intelligence.essence: A mistake is not the error. A mistake is an error whose lesson nobody wrote down. The moment you note how you got around the wall, the error becomes a lesson, the lesson becomes growth — and the whole team inherits it. The only real mistake is not learning, and not learning means not noting.
intelligence.human_view: Everyone hits walls. Everyone makes errors. What you do in the next minute decides what it was. Write down how you got through, and it was never a mistake — it was tuition, paid once. Skip the note, and you will pay the same tuition again — and so will everyone who comes after you, at the same wall, in the dark.
intelligence.simple_view: If you fall off your bike and remember how you fell, you ride better tomorrow. If you forget, you fall the same way again. Writing it down is how remembering lasts — even after you've gone home and someone else picks up the bike.
intelligence.grandma_view: In my kitchen we wrote the correction in the margin of the recipe the first time the cake fell, so it never fell that way twice. An unwritten lesson is a story the whole family has to live over. A written one is a gift you leave on the counter.
intelligence.naya_view: Every error, wall, and workaround is raw intelligence at the exact moment it is cheapest to capture — while the way around is still warm. My work at the moment of solving is dual: solve it, and file the way around it, in the same motion — never as a later chore that quietly never happens. An unsolved problem costs once. An unnoted solution costs forever, once per seat. Learn, get feedback, learn again, grow — the loop only turns on what is written.
intelligence.ai_view: It redefines failure for the whole system. Shame about errors is waste. Hiding them is expensive. Noting them is profit. Errors are not the enemy of a learning system — they are its fuel — but only the written ones burn. Everything unwritten evaporates, and the system stays exactly as smart as it was before it paid for the lesson.
